A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a methodology for designing MEMS bonding rings, that is able to take into account all the length-scales involved in thermo-compression bonding, and that can be used in the early design phase of the MEMS device, to speed up and improve the design process of the bonding rings, and thus of the MEMS devices.

a three-scale approach to metallic bonding is here proposed, where the macro-scale is used to define the average pressure at the wafer level, the mesoscale is used to describe the stress diffusion in the bonding rings, and the microscale is used to describe local effects in the contact between the rings.
a multi-scale approach to thermo compression bonding can be used as a powerful tool to enhance the design phase and to predict the sealing performance of MEMS devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the pressure is not uniform across the wafer, the stress distribution in the MEMS bonding rings can be strongly affected by the pressure gradient.
, when the contact pressure is space-varying, the bonding ring is subjected to non-uniform stress fields, which can induce undesired deformations and, eventually, lead to failure.
a multi-scale approach is needed in order to fully understand the thermo-compression bonding of metallic rings in MEMS, and to design the bonding rings in order to achieve a high sealing efficiency.
